items.title: Researchers identify dimensionality as key factor in large language models' poor performance on tabular prediction tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Why Large Language Models Fail at Tabular Prediction
items.summary: A study examines why large language models (LLMs) struggle with predictive analytics on tabular data, a common machine learning task. Researchers tested five hypotheses for this failure and found that increasing input dimensionality significantly reduces LLM accuracy, unlike classical models whose performance remains stable or improves. The study involved controlled experiments on 31 benchmark datasets and comparisons with 252 classical models, revealing that LLMs behave like local, distance-based methods in low dimensions but fail to replicate classical model predictions in higher dimensions. The findings explain why LLMs underperform on tabular data despite their success in other areas, while the internal mechanisms behind this limitation remain unclear.

items.summary:
OpenAI announced ten significant advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science achieved by an internal AI model called Astra, which resolved or made substantial progress on longstanding open problems across various fields including geometry, coding theory, group theory, and quantum complexity. These results were formalized and prepared into manuscripts with human assistance, and OpenAI has released the AI's narrated reasoning for each solution.

The advances include new bounds on sphere packing and binary codes, the construction of non-sofic groups, disproof of Connes's rigidity conjecture, lower bounds in arithmetic circuit complexity, a quantum parallel repetition theorem, hardness results for the closest vector problem, and solutions to several Erdős problems in combinatorics and graph theory. OpenAI emphasizes responsible attribution of AI contributions and encourages the mathematical community to engage with these results as AI systems evolve as research collaborators.

items.originalTitle: Show HN: Ex-Deloitte auditor open-sourced the whole SOC 2 method for your AI
items.summary:
A former Deloitte auditor has published an open-source SOC 2 readiness and audit methodology specifically designed for artificial intelligence systems. The repository includes a comprehensive control library, test attributes, evidence mapping, and detailed rules for Type II testing, aiming to provide transparency and rigor in AI compliance processes.

The methodology features 86 controls, 355 test attributes, and 498 calibration examples that illustrate judgment calls made during audits, all based on synthetic scenarios to protect client confidentiality. It emphasizes complete population testing over sampling where possible, with mechanisms to ensure data completeness and unbiased selection when sampling is necessary.

This open-source approach seeks to replace traditional compliance methods that rely on trust by providing detailed, machine-verifiable criteria and examples, potentially improving the reliability and transparency of SOC 2 audits for AI applications.

items.summary:
A recent analysis argues that the reported AI-driven revenue growth for Amazon, Google, and Microsoft primarily stems from the compute spending of two unprofitable AI labs, Anthropic and OpenAI, which rely heavily on tens of billions of dollars in funding. Despite claims of AI paying off, these hyperscalers have not broken out AI-specific revenues and have increased prices or bundled AI features to boost cloud segment growth.

The report highlights that Google, Amazon, and Microsoft have invested heavily in data centers and infrastructure largely to support Anthropic and OpenAI, with Google investing up to $40 billion in Anthropic and Amazon funneling $50 billion into OpenAI. Microsoft has dedicated data centers to OpenAI and disclosed spending over $100 billion on its OpenAI relationship. The analysis suggests that without the compute spend from these two AI labs, the hyperscalers may lack a substantial AI business.

items.originalTitle: When AI Benchmarks Plateau: A Systematic Study of Benchmark Saturation
items.summary:
A recent study systematically examines benchmark saturation in artificial intelligence, focusing on 60 language model benchmarks and identifying 14 properties related to saturation. The research finds that nearly half of these benchmarks exhibit performance plateaus, with saturation rates increasing as benchmarks age, which complicates model differentiation and reduces long-term evaluation value.

The study also reveals that expert curation, rather than public test data availability, influences a benchmark's resilience to saturation. These findings suggest that careful design choices can extend the useful lifespan of AI benchmarks and support the development of more durable evaluation methods.

The AI-generated images included historical and cultural references such as former Chancellor Helmut Kohl, the World Trade Center after 9/11, and a German reunification postage stamp, which puzzled some spectators.

Festival organizers described the AI as an image-generating force creating a dynamic visual backdrop around the singers, who remained the fixed point on stage. The projections were curated by Marcus Lobbes and his team, drawing from pre-selected images and previous Wagner performances. Two more performances with AI-assisted staging are scheduled at the festival.

While AI offers genuine utility across various fields, its limitations and the speculative nature of some investments have raised warning signs among market observers.

The report compares the AI investment surge to past phenomena like bitcoin, noting inflated valuations and unrealistic expectations such as rapid wealth creation and a near-future abundance driven by AI automation. Market indicators include unusual premiums on ADRs of companies like SK Hynix and TSMC, suggesting investor enthusiasm may be outpacing fundamental value. Experts caution that despite expanding AI infrastructure, investors should be wary of speculative excesses and maintain realistic assessments of AI's current capabilities and economic returns.

Her framework seeks to guide teams through stages of AI maturity to better realize the benefits of AI integration in engineering processes.

items.summary:
Palantir is truly the Nvidia of AI software. On Monday, the company delivered another rip-roaring quarterly result, showing revenue up a blistering 93%, well ahead of what it had projected. The company has accelerated revenue growth every quarter for three years, from a 13% rate of expansion in the second quarter of 2023. In that time, Palantir’s top line has increased from $533 million a quarter to $1.9 billion. Palantir stock rose 11% in after-hours trading.

Its growth over the past three years isn’t quite as dazzling as that of Nvidia—whose stranglehold on the AI chip market lifted revenue to $216 billion in its most recent fiscal year from $27 billion three years earlier—but it’s pretty stunning nevertheless. What makes this particularly notable is that Palantir doesn’t develop its own large language models. It has figured out how to make a massive amount of money—Palantir’s operations generated $2.1 billion in cash in the first half of 2026, while capital expenditures were only $22 million—from software that works on top of other companies’ AI.

items.originalTitle: Google DeepMind Exec Says Unprecedented Capex Is Actually a Bet On ‘RSI’
items.summary:
Over the weekend, Jasjeet Sekhon, the chief strategy officer at Google’s DeepMind AI unit, used two words to describe what needs to happen to justify his industry’s unprecedented capital expenditures: recursive self-improvement. The white-hot term refers to AI that can automatically create better versions of itself.

RSI is a “key part of the investment thesis,” Sekhon said at the Agentic AI Summit, which took place at the University of California-Berkeley.

RSI is the new AGI (artificial general intelligence) in the sense that it’s all anyone in the field is talking about as the industry’s next goalpost. Whether RSI would precede or coincide with AGI—AI that is better than humans at most economically valuable tasks—is an entirely different conversation!

To be fair to Sekhon, RSI has been an industry goal for some time. I first started hearing the term from researchers in early 2023. But it wasn’t part of corporations’ public rhetoric until recent weeks.

items.title: How an Apple iCloud Policy Fueled Employee Leaks Ahead of OpenAI Suit
items.originalTitle: How an Apple iCloud Policy Fueled Employee Leaks Ahead of OpenAI Suit
items.summary:
In a lawsuit early last month, Apple accused former employees who are now at OpenAI of stealing a trove of trade secrets from the iPhone maker—in part by improperly accessing confidential Apple documents after they left the company. Even before the suit was filed, some of the more than 400 former Apple employees who now work at OpenAI began receiving stern letters from Apple lawyers informing them they were in possession of confidential Apple material, people familiar with the matter said.

But the reason many of them had access to that material was due to an Apple policy, not because the former employees were attempting to steal its secrets, the people said. The issue: Even though Apple kicked them off most of its corporate systems after they resigned, the former employees continued to have access to Apple files shared with them when they still worked there.
